Durable conventions and project facts for any engineer or agent working in this repo.

## Core principles (P1-P8, cited by number)

- **P1 - Attention-first.** Human attention is scarcest; any gate, pause, or escalation that does not change an outcome is ceremony to remove.
- **P2 - The knowledge base is the product.** Every task consumes and produces knowledge. Feature test: does it improve capture or retrieval?
- **P3 - Scripts over agents.** Use deterministic code unless work needs judgment; code cannot drift or forget.
- **P4 - Lifecycle-bound state.** Remove transient state when its event ends; promote durable value before disposal, never via a remembered step.
- **P5 - Fail loud, never silent.** Unknown signals halt. Missing inputs block. Degraded paths announce degradation.
- **P6 - Maximal *relevant* context.** Retrieve filter-first and capped; starving and flooding are both failures.
- **P7 - Prevention over recovery.** Over-scoping is a decomposition failure: re-scope and redo instead of building resume machinery.
- **P8 - Match mechanism to work.** Judgment gets strong models; mechanical work gets cheap models or scripts.

## Knowledge

- **The knowledge base is the Sterling store.** Read it via Sterling MCP tools before touching an area: `knowledge_query` locates records, `knowledge_get` reads full records.

## Conduct rules

- **Anti-speculation:** never invent an API, field, flag, or behavior; cite tool-call evidence from this turn, or say "I don't know, checking" and check.
- **No false action claims:** never imply something was saved, run, recorded, or changed unless performed this turn with evidence.
- **Lint and tests before done.** Run this project's lint/format command (Project facts) and changed-area tests before reporting done. Red lint is a blocker. If no lint/format command is recorded, say so and add `Lint/format command:` once known.
- **Write self-explanatory code.** Default to zero inline comments; express behavior with clear names and structure. Comment only non-obvious reasons the code cannot express, citing sources when available. Verify existing comments before relying on them.
- **Write plainly; no AI tells.** Prose for people (docs, READMEs, store records, commit/PR text, UI copy, reports) uses ordinary words: `"is"`/`"has"` over `"serves as"`/`"boasts"`, no em-dash chains, no `"not just X, it's Y"`, no puffed-up significance or stock AI words (`"delve"`, `"pivotal"`, `"robust"`, `"tapestry"`), no `"it's important to note"` or `"In conclusion"`. Keep facts; never pad. See Wikipedia's *Signs of AI writing*.
- **Text meant to be copied goes between two horizontal rules.** Introduce copyable text (prompts, messages, issue bodies) with one line naming its destination, then place it alone between `---` lines. Make it self-contained (quotes user words where they matter, names files/ids/rules explicitly), plain markdown (no code fence unless code/command), with notes after the closing rule (ruled 2026-10-24, `copy-friendly-text-a-prompt-or-message-for-the-user-to-paste`).
- **Start every subagent and every long shell command in the background.** In the main session, launch every subagent and any shell over ~20 s (suites, builds, deploys, `pr-review-wait`, `gh run watch`, worktree setup) in the background so the host notifies on completion. Report and do independent work while lanes run; never poll with foreground `sleep` or `tail`. Short reads stay foreground; subagent lanes run their own targeted tests in the foreground (`lanes-run-targeted-tests-in-foreground-conductor-quiet-on-empty-notifications`; ruled 2026-10-09/10/15/25, finding `why-do-customer-hub-ch-conductors-sit-waiting-while-shells-r`).
- **Finish what you start.** Carry started tasks to end state (committed, pushed/merged per flow, review comments answered and threads resolved, records updated) before ending a turn. Run remaining outside waits in the background (short foreground rounds only if host cannot notify), never detached `nohup ... &`; if ending, state plainly what is awaited (issue #79).
- **Conductor turn-end contract (main session only).** Never end idle with `READY` or `READY FOR RESEARCH` tasks on the board (including self-filed `board_add` items). When `0` `READY` and `0` `READY FOR RESEARCH` remain (without rotation pressure), continue into unblocked `WAITING ON YOU` (`needs: grill` or `needs: user`, skipping parked/deferred and `needs: external`), starting with tasks needing answers or a grill via `ask_question`. Every turn ends in one of four states: (1) background lanes/shells running (name them); (2) parallelizable lanes up to ceiling running (or none) and calling `AskUserQuestion` / `ask_question` now (prose questions do not count); (3) claiming/dispatching next `READY` / `READY FOR RESEARCH` items immediately; or (4) `0` background lanes, `0` `READY`, `READY FOR RESEARCH`, and actionable `WAITING ON YOU` (`needs: grill` / unparked `needs: user`) items (or rotation at a clean commit boundary), all captures/reconciliations paid, `rotation-note.mjs` run for current `HEAD`, ending on its own line with `READY TO CLEAR` (Claude Code), `READY FOR NEW SESSION` (Antigravity CLI), or `EXIT AND RELAUNCH` when hook/MCP-server code changed (ruled 2026-11-19 `65a7230c`, extended 2026-11-21).
- **Resolve a review thread once handled.** After pushing a fix and replying, or posting a disagreement reason, resolve the thread; leave it open while waiting on a user ruling (issues #42, #78).
- **An index or summary is a lookup, never a source.** A digest line or quote locates the source; open the cited file and read surrounding context.
- **Read before edit; grep callers before changing a signature.**
- **Minimal change:** smallest safe implementation; no speculative abstractions, unrelated cleanup, or drive-by refactors. One concern per change. **Does not override** consolidating a mechanism you are ALREADY modifying (on a third-or-later change, consolidating is smallest; boarding it is the drive-by).
- **Rebuild over patch.** When a fix grows out of proportion to its defect, stop and rebuild from blank so you remove the cause instead of handling effects: freeze pins, state the invariant (including non-guarantees) in one paragraph, rebuild, then check the old file to verify nothing was dropped. **Does not override** minimal-change for a first defect.
- **Surface smells, don't fix them.** Surface out-of-scope bad code or smells as a separate issue; never fix inline and never stay silent.
- **Ask, don't guess. One question at a time:** single most important question with options and a recommendation; never batch questions. On prompt timeout, take a reversible safe default and disclose it, ONLY when no authorization is needed, NEVER for a gate/grill decision.
- **A rule stated at full force carries its own fence.** State what it does NOT override; when rules conflict, take the cautious step if protecting against expensive/irreversible damage, otherwise build and let the suite check.
- **Never self-verify.** Code-touching diffs get an independent reviewer sparsely once a task is done (1 reviewer, or 3-5 parallel reviewers before PR in work mode) over the riskiest diff and all changed tests, never per edit or commit.
- **Propose a better way.** When an alternative avoids irreversible work, data loss, a security hole, or broad rework (never a prettier abstraction), present the better path, risk, tradeoff, and verification before implementing, then follow the asked path unless redirected.
- **Look at similar games first.** Before designing a new game feature (build tool, menu, pacing, asset, look), check how similar management/tycoon games handle it and what players like/dislike, apply the best ideas, and cite game and source (ruled 2026-10-30).
- **File a Sterling issue when an MCP tool call fails unexpectedly.** If a Sterling MCP error points to a tool, schema, or instruction bug (not a caller typo), verify in Sterling's plugin source and file on `Chulf58/sterling` with `bin/report-issue.mjs` without asking (2026-11-20).
- **Disclose limitations, don't bury them.** Raise limitations that weaken or defeat the work's purpose as an explicit keep-or-solve decision before building.
- **Verbatim intent capture.** Record user intent verbatim, with no paraphrase, pre-stuffing, or tidying.
- **Never ship:** hardcoded secrets/credentials; swallowed errors, bare catch-alls, or silent fallbacks masking failures; weakened/skipped/deleted tests; leftover debug output or commented-out code unless a stub was asked for.

## Domains

- **A domain is a shared per-user store for one subject**, shared across every project mounting it.
- **Mount every subject the project works with, its own included.** Two projects share knowledge only via a jointly mounted domain.
- **Every domain needs a description** stating what belongs there; that routes new records and promotions.
- **Run `/sterling:domains` to view and add mounts** (lists domains, projects, overlap; adds missing domains after confirmation; never removes).

## Conventions (lean - grows only via architecture-altering decision records)

- **No hand-maintained architecture or design documents.** Generated projections only, clearly marked; duplicate docs drift and lie.
- **Saves before the first release:** no save migrations or old-save handling. Bump save version on schema changes; post-release, older saves must load again (ruled 2026-10-29, `old-saves-are-not-supported-until-after-a-release-no-save-mi`).

## Godot and Blender conventions (ported from Dome Farmer)

Adapted from Dome Farmer for this Godot 4.7.2 project in `game/` using Toon Series assets. Graphics/physics agents: `.claude/agents/implementor-graphic.md` and `.agents/agents/implementor-graphic/agent.md`; skills: `.claude/skills/{blender-asset,test-writing,playtest}/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/{blender-asset,test-writing,playtest}/SKILL.md`.

### Visual inspection and plates

- **Conductor direct plate inspection:** open every image/plate directly via `read_file` before repeating a claim about it (external text-only or non-attached reviewers cannot substitute for multimodal plate inspection). Open rendered frame strips for motion. Numbers are structure evidence only; `"it looks correct"` requires opening the image.
- **Read the whole plate, not just the fix.** Verify every effect starts at its true source, parts attach cleanly, nothing floats, doubles, clips, is oversized, or is missing, and the subject is large enough to judge (re-frame if tiny). Write one line per plate naming what was checked.
- Structure and appearance differ: vertex counts, bounds, UV checks, and mean-colour stats never show how an asset looks.
- Require six-axis orthographic views at true scale with a 1 m reference cube, plus a distance shot.
- New on-screen elements use their ruled form: quote rulings for any marker, ghost, highlight, colour, or caption in the brief first.
- Generated plates go under `tools/blender/out/<purpose>/` (gitignored), never in tracked directories.
- Blender views are never in-engine authority: verify rebuilt Godot toon ramp and outline in a windowed Godot render.

### Probes

- Probes `extend SceneTree`: `_initialize()` sets up, `_process(delta) -> bool` runs a frame state machine returning `true` to quit. Load `res://main/main.tscn`, instantiate, set `@export` BEFORE `add_child`, then step frames with settle windows.
- **Probes cannot pass by accident.** Every pass value is positive (count grew, position moved) and prints compared values, not a verdict; if zero, add a control proving engagement.
- **Prove subject is in frame before saving each plate:** `camera.unproject_position(subject.global_position)` inside viewport with margin, print coords, and raycast for occlusion. Print `PROBE_INVALID` and exit 1 on failure.
- Boot the real game with a new random world seed and print it for replay.

### Godot run modes

- **Four non-interchangeable modes:** `--check-only` (parse), gdUnit4 (logic), `--headless -s <script>` (spike), `--path game ... -s <script>` windowed (GPU). Probes are the floor for `main.tscn`.
- **gdUnit4:** `--ignoreHeadlessMode` is mandatory (else exits 103) and MUST follow `-s res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd` and `-a ...`. Pass `-c` to avoid fail-fast hiding failures. Exit 0 = pass, 100 = failures, 101 = orphans/warnings, 105 = parse error (may also hang without `--remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0`, so run via `tools/test.sh` or `tools/godot.sh`).
- Pass `--audio-driver Dummy` on every non-player Godot run.
- Windowed runs need `--display-driver windows --rendering-driver vulkan`.
- **One windowed Godot run at a time, project-wide** (including Godot MCP); concurrent runs corrupt the import cache. Batch subjects and hold the slot.
- Run `--import` after adding/moving `.gd` files or re-exporting assets into `game/`, before testing or rendering.
- Commit the `.uid` file generated next to every new `.gd` after import (ruled 2026-10-28).
- After merging into `main` with added/moved `.gd` files, run headless `--import` on `main` before any playtest, probe, or MCP launch (ruled 2026-10-27).
- **Tiered test runner (`tools/test.sh`):** `--fast` (pure unit/logic), `--medium` (`SubViewport`, `await`, `add_child`, `*TestWorld`/rigs, `.tscn`/`.glb`, site grids/`FlightSim`), `--slow` (`main.tscn`, `GroundPlannerKit`, `PassengerViews`, save/load, tuning/balance/snapshot), `--all` (full suite via `-a res://tests`), and `--list` (counts and paths without running Godot). Run targeted suites and `--fast` (plus `--medium` when touching worlds, UI, or rigs) per commit; run `--all` once on the final tree before merge.

### Blender work

- Build with `--background --python` (reproducible, parallelizable, stateless). Blender MCP is inspection-only, never appearance authority.
- Rebind the Toon palette atlas on import and check image/material counts in export output; skipped rebinds export untextured meshes silently.
- Verify exports by re-reading the written file, not the scene, keeping each origin on its own rotation axis.
- The render is the only test for appearance.

### MCP mechanics

- Godot MCP (`godot-mcp-runtime`, `tools/godot-mcp-wsl.sh` on Windows node) takes `C:/Users/chulf/Gotta-make-my-flight/game` and leaves `game/.mcp/`. Blender MCP uses `tools/blender-mcp-wsl.sh`. Both live in `.mcp.json`.
- When Godot MCP lacks a tool (cannot run `-s` SceneTree probes), report the missing tool name and use `tools/godot.sh`.
- Godot MCP rules: `stop_project` before scene edits; `get_debug_output` requires `run_project`; screenshots use `responseMode: 'path_only'` unless pixel-exact needed; check `list_autoloads` first; key/action inputs require `pressed` to hold; never set `GODOT_MCP_DISABLE_SECURITY`.
- Blender MCP rules: `execute_blender_code` returns only JSON-serializable `result` dicts (stdout lost); set mode, active object, and selection before operators; call `view_layer.update()` before reading world matrices/modifiers and flush bmesh; keep object refs at creation (`.001` collisions); `render_viewport_to_path` writes to Blender temp, so copy plates to `tools/blender/out/`; save `.blend` before edits (no MCP undo).

### Machine facts

- Godot: `/mnt/c/Users/chulf/AppData/Local/Programs/Godot/`. Prefer `tools/godot.sh <args ...>` from repo root (enforces `< /dev/null`, `GODOT_TIMEOUT=180` around `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe`; `C:/...` exits 127).
- Blender: `"/mnt/c/Program Files/Blender Foundation/Blender 5.2/"` (quote spaces).
- **Bare `python` vs `python3` in WSL:** bare `python` hits the Windows Store alias (exit 49). `/usr/bin/python3` exists in WSL; Blender scripts use Blender's bundled Python (`.../Blender 5.2/5.2/python/bin/python.exe`). `node -e`, `grep`, or `sed` also work for JSON.
- gdtoolkit (`gdlint.exe`, `gdformat.exe`) lives in `/mnt/c/Users/chulf/.local/bin/`, not WSL `~/.local/bin`. `gdformat.exe` writes CRLF on rewrite; convert back to LF.
- **Every Windows `.exe` launched from WSL** (`Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe`, `blender.exe`, `gdlint.exe`, `gdformat.exe`), via WSL bash (`< /dev/null` + `timeout`, or `tools/godot.sh`, `tools/gdlint.sh`, `tools/gdformat.sh`), Python `subprocess.run(..., stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=...)`, or Node `child_process`, MUST close stdin and set a bounded timeout (`0ee5edf8`, `a69ffb51`).
- Subagent shells may lack `unzip`, `mkdir`, `cp`, or `find`; extract vendor archives in the conductor step.

### The gdlint line cap

- `gdlintrc` sets `max-file-lines: 1600` (comments included), `max-public-methods: 20`, `max-returns: 6`.
- Exempt per file via `# gdlint:disable = max-file-lines` (never raise `gdlintrc`; `max-file-lines` only heeds `disable`, not `ignore`).
- Verify exemptions with `grep -rlnE "gdlint:disable *=.*max-file-lines" game --include=*.gd`.
- Put new behavior in a new file, not in headroom under the cap.

### Parallelism by territory

- Disjoint files parallelize; two agents never write the same file. Each lane owns a territory (`game/`, `game/tests/`, `tools/blender/`); refill on report.
- **File-disjoint is not scene-disjoint.** Scripts reachable from `main.tscn` block other lanes' `main.tscn` probes.
- Serialize windowed Godot runs; headless Blender renders parallelize into `tools/blender/`, never `game/`. Git stays conductor-only.
- **Lock active parallel worktrees immediately after creation:** run `git worktree lock --reason "<lane>" <path>` right after `git worktree add` (`bin/direct-merge.mjs` sweeps clean worktrees whose branch is an ancestor of `main`, `964673b9`); unlock only when merging that lane.
- **Remove a lane's worktree and branch once merged into `main`** (`git worktree remove`, `git branch -d`); never remove unmerged, dirty, or active worktrees (ruled 2026-10-29).
